brief.ask: Set the art direction for 36 high-end wedding evites as a coherent luxury line, not 36 one-offs. Decide the families (we explored watercolor botanicals, painted Italian villas, art deco emerald and gold) and what the motion layer does that paper never could, without becoming a gimmick.
brief.audience: Couples choosing a stationery suite; guests from 20 to 90.
brief.feeling: The weight of letterpress and the light of a candlelit room, in a phone.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.
Must sit beside the best paper stationery studios and win.
references: Exploration grid A: fine-art watercolor garden roses, peonies, olive and eucalyptus forming arches on deckled cotton paper with gold-foil flecks; flat-lay on silk and brass trays.
Exploration grid B: gouache Italian villa terraces, arched colonnades, cypress, lemon trees in terracotta, bougainvillea, golden-hour hills.
Exploration grid C: deep emerald marble with art deco gold linework frames, crescent moons and fine constellations; symmetrical and grand.

proposals.title: The Measure Before the Mark
proposals.idea: Every one of the 36 designs derives all proportion, all type scale, all foil vector, and all motion timing from a single declared harmonic ratio — a cantus firmus chosen per family and never negotiated away — so the line reads as one scored work, not a catalogue.
proposals.geometry: A single proportional canon governs each family: Botanical uses the golden section (1:1.618) dividing the plate into a dominant floral mass and a subordinate text field, with a ruled gutter of exactly one unit separating them — the deckled edge of the generated paper always falls on that boundary. Villa uses a 3:2 tripartite column grid mirroring an actual colonnade bay, so the architectural arches in the image ARE the grid. Deco uses a strict 8-column symmetrical lattice anchored to a central axis, all ornamental linework derived from that axis by rotation and reflection — no element placed by eye alone. Within each family the 12 designs vary content, not structure: the ratio holds across all 36 plates. Cards sit in a 9:16 phone-native vertical, with a 24px minimum safe margin on all sides that the text layer never violates.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) in three optical sizes: a display cut at 52–64px for names, a text cut at 18–20px for venue and date, a caption cut at 12–13px for ceremony details — three registers, not two, because hierarchy requires a third term. Tracking: display at –10 to –20 (tight, letterpress register); text at 0; caption at +80 (breath before the fine print). All set in upper-and-lower, never all-caps for names — the cap height is earned by being the tallest element in a field of ascenders, not by shouting. Cormorant's italic is used only for the venue name, one departure that earns its distinctness. IM Fell English (OFL, Google Fonts) is the backup for the Deco family's inline ornamental numerals, where Cormorant's figures read too clean.
proposals.imageLogic: All 36 art plates are generative (Magnific grid, two prompt runs of 16 plates each, selecting 12 per family). Prompt discipline: each run specifies the proportional canon explicitly — 'golden-section composition, dominant mass in upper 61.8% of frame, text field implied in lower 38.2%, deckled cotton-paper substrate, single motivated light source at 35° azimuth upper-left, no centred symmetry except in Deco family.' The image does not contain text. The foreground cut-out layer (botanicals, balustrade columns, constellation arcs) is generated separately against transparency, prompted to sit inside the subordinate field so it never occludes the type zone — the grid enforces this, not the editor's eye in post. Light in every plate is motivated: one source, one direction, stated in the prompt and consistent across all 12 plates in a family so that foil vectors and bokeh origins are not arbit
proposals.texture: Botanical: simulated 300gsm Fabriano cotton-rag tooth, generated as a displacement layer — not a photo scan, a procedurally generated heightmap baked into the Magnific prompt as 'fine grain, visible laid-lines, slight cockle at wet-edge botanicals.' Gold-foil flecks are WebGL fragments anchored to the motivated light vector, not scattered. Villa: warm ochre-tinted gouache ground, brush-stroke edge visible at colonnade margins, terracotta shadow under arches — all generated, all physically plausible under the declared light. Deco: cold emerald marble generated with vein direction matching the 8-column grid's diagonals — the geology is not decorative, it participates in the structure.
proposals.motion: Motion is earned in three acts and never decorates before it explains. Act 1 (0–0.8s, on load): the art plate resolves from soft focus to full detail — a depth-of-field rack, not a fade, because a fade has no spatial implication and a rack names a distance. Act 2 (0.8–2.0s): foreground cut-outs drift into position along the proportional grid lines at 0.4px/frame eased with a gentle spring — they arrive in the order the motivated light would logically illuminate them: nearest plane first, deepest last. Act 3 (continuous, after 2.0s): WebGL foil shimmer responds only to phone tilt, highlight vector locked to the 35° motivated light — tilting toward the source brightens, away dims, exactly as physical foil under a candle would. Bokeh particles (Botanical only) drift upward at 0.3px/s, not looping — they reach the top and stop, because a loop would deny that time has passed. Candle-flicker (
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt runs: Run 1 targets Botanical and Villa (16-plate grid, 8 per family, selecting 12 final across both). Run 2 targets Deco (16-plate grid, selecting 12). Each prompt encodes: substrate, light source azimuth and elevation, proportional field division, foreground cut-out separation flag, no embedded text. Cut-out foreground layers are a second Magnific pass on selected plates with 'isolated on transparency, same light source' — Magnific's background-removal pipeline handles separation. WebGL shader is written once, parameterised by: foil-vector azimuth (matches plate), bokeh density (0 for Deco, medium for Villa, high for Botanical), flicker frequency. Tela document template is built once per family — same layer stack, same type zones, same motion timing — then the art plate and cut-outs are swapped. The 12 designs per family are 12 plate swaps into one template, not 12
proposals.humanTrace: The harmonic ratio is chosen by a human before any image is generated — it is the decision that cannot be automated. The motivated light source azimuth is declared in writing before the first prompt is submitted, and every subsequent decision (foil vector, parallax gain, cut-out arrival order) is checked against it by a person, not an algorithm. Editorial selection from the 16-plate grid is a human act of compositional judgment: does the generated image's mass actually fall in the upper 61.8%? Does the deckled edge land on the gutter? Plates that fail the structural test are discarded even if they are beautiful. That is the human trace: a prior constraint, held.
proposals.risk: The proportional canon will occasionally fight a generated image that wants to be differently composed — Magnific does not guarantee golden-section mass distribution, and some plates will need to be re-prompted or cropped, adding iteration cost. The deeper risk is that rigour reads as coldness: a wedding invitation that feels like a theorem. That risk is worth taking because every competitor in the luxury stationery space is selling atmosphere without structure, and atmosphere without structure does not age — it dates. A line that can be explained by a single ratio in ten years is a line that still has authority in ten years. The warmth is carried by the texture and the motivated light; the structure is what makes the warmth legible as intention rather than accident.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the reveal to announce itself — a swell, a held beat, a moment of conscious surprise. I expect a proposal where the motion layer performs the drama explicitly, where the foreground elements arrive with flourish rather than in the quiet order that light would dictate. My disagreement is structural: a reveal that announces itself is a reveal that has decided its own i

proposals.title: Proof Before the Run
proposals.idea: Every card is a ghost of a physical act — a misregistered overprint, a pulled proof, an ink drag — so the motion layer does not animate a scene but replays the making of the object itself, and guests feel the press before they read the name.
proposals.geometry: Portrait, 9:19.5 phone-native ratio. The compositional engine is a registration-cross grid — four quadrants defined by a hairline crosshair at optical center, the way a printer's forme is locked. Each family offsets its art plate slightly from dead-center (2–6px deliberate misregister) so the foreground cut-outs never sit perfectly on top; the gap is the evidence. No centered symmetry for its own sake: the text block sits in the lower-left quadrant, weighted like a colophon, never centered. Margins are unequal: wider at foot than head, wider at fore-edge than spine — a book proportion, not a poster proportion.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (OFL/Google Fonts) for all display: names at 28–34px tracked at -10, uppercase small-cap for the date line. Body copy — venue, time, RSVP — in DM Mono at 11px, tracked +40, because a proof sheet always has a typewritten annotation beside the beautiful plate. The two faces are in explicit tension and that tension is the design. No script typefaces: the hand is already in the image, it does not need to be performed again in the font.
proposals.imageLogic: Three families, each with its own plate grammar. Family A (Botanical Proof): Magnific prompt directs a 4×3 draft grid — 12 distinct plates — of fine-art botanical overprints: rose, peony, olive, eucalyptus rendered as if two Risograph passes are 1–3px out of register, deckled paper tooth visible at edges, random gold-ink droplets that are not decorative but are evidence of a flood-ink moment. Family B (Villa Trace): 8-plate grid of gouache Italian villa terraces rendered as if photographed from a working architect's study — cyan construction lines ghost under the warm gouache, cypress silhouettes are a separate plate layer so they drift on tilt independently. Family C (Deco Proof Sheet): 8-plate grid of deep emerald marble grounds with art deco gold linework drawn as if silk-screened — the gold rule is slightly heavier at the pull-start corner, thinning across the card, recording the squ
proposals.texture: Simulated cotton-rag paper tooth baked into the plate at generation (prompt instructs visible fiber direction, 300gsm weight, slight surface undulation). A thin film-grain shader layer (procedural, 8–12% opacity, grain size 1.4px) sits over the WebGL canvas at all times — not toggled off on hover, because the grain is the surface, not a mood. Foil shimmer in the WebGL layer is not a full-bleed mirror: it appears only on the gold linework and the hairline crosshair, because foil is expensive and printers only put it where it earns its keep.
proposals.motion: 0ms: plate arrives at full opacity, no fade — it was already printed. 0–200ms: the registration crosshair hairlines draw in from center outward, as if the press arm is locking. 200–600ms: the misregistered foreground botanical or architectural cut-out drifts 3px onto its ground, settling into imperfect register — this is the only motion that reads as 'animation' and it completes, it does not loop. 600ms onward: tilt parallax holds — the foreground cut-out drifts ±6px on gyroscope input, the midground plate ±2px, the text layer fixed. The parallax gap between layers is the permanent visible record of the misregister. Candle-flicker bokeh in WebGL fires only on the gold linework, 0.4Hz, amplitude 4% — it reads as the foil catching a draft, not as a particle system. Reduced-motion: crosshair draw-in replaced by a static hairline; parallax disabled; bokeh static. Nothing is lost because the
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific draft-grid prompts cover all three families: Prompt 1 returns a 4×3 grid (12 plates) for Family A Botanical Proof and Family B Villa Trace variants. Prompt 2 returns a 2×4 grid (8 plates) for Family C Deco Proof Sheet variants. Editorial selection from those 20 plates populates 36 slots — some plates repeat across two cards with different foreground cut-out layers, which is honest because a print shop runs the same plate twice for different editions. Foreground cut-outs (botanicals, cypress, architectural fragments) are generated as separate Magnific passes with white-ground isolation, then masked in Tela. The registration crosshair, hairline gold rules, and grain shader are procedural GLSL — no image asset. DM Mono and Cormorant Garamond are loaded from Google Fonts. Total generative cost: two prompt grids plus four foreground cut-out passes.
proposals.humanTrace: The deliberate misregister — 2–6px offset between plate and cut-out layer — is the trace. It is not a glitch effect. It is the record of a decision: someone chose not to correct it because correcting it would erase the evidence that two things were printed separately. The crosshair draw-in animation replays the act of locking registration. The grain shader does not simulate age; it simulates the surface the ink sat on. The squeegee-weight variation in the gold rule is baked into the plate at generation by prompting 'variable stroke pressure, heavier at upper-left origin.' Every guest who tilts their phone and watches the cypress drift 4px from the villa wall is feeling the tolerance stack of a layered print.
proposals.risk: The misregister will read as a mistake to some couples and to some colleagues on this team. A client who paid for luxury stationery may ask why it is not aligned. The answer — that misregister is the proof of layering, that correcting it would erase the evidence of making — requires the sales surface to explain the concept, which is a real commercial liability. The risk is worth it because every other direction in this room will be beautiful and resolved, and this one will be the only direction where the guest can feel that something was done to the card rather than rendered for it. That difference is what separates letterpress from offset, and it is what this brief asked for.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will call the misregister noise and the DM Mono annotation clutter and will want to strip to plate plus one face. That move would produce something elegant and legible and completely without evidence of process. I am not adding the crosshair and the typewriter annotation for decoration — I am adding them because a proof sheet has a proof sheet's marks, and removing them produces a b

proposals.title: Light as Generative Contract
proposals.idea: A single declared light source at 35°/22° upper-left becomes the generative axiom from which every visual parameter — foil shimmer vector, parallax gain per depth plane, bokeh falloff origin, shadow offset, candle-flicker timing — is derived as a logical consequence, not an aesthetic choice, so that all 36 designs behave as one coherent physical instrument tuned to three material families.
proposals.geometry: Three families (Botanical, Villa, Deco) each governed by a shared depth-plane contract: foreground cut-outs on plane Z+1, art plate on Z0, bokeh field on Z-1. Within each family, a 12-card grid subdivides by aspect lock — 9:19.5 portrait, 4px safe margin at 390px — so the card never reflows. Family identity lives in the art plate silhouette language: botanical arches are asymmetric and organic; villa cards use a strict colonnade module — two vertical rule columns flanking a centred aperture — that echoes the arched portico; deco cards are radially symmetric from a single vanishing point, gold linework radiating outward. The three geometries are materially incompatible by design: you cannot mistake a botanical for a deco card even in greyscale.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) at display: 28–34px, tracked +60 for venue name, set in small-caps, upper-case; weight shifts from Light (botanical) to SemiBold (deco) to signal family register. Body and date line: DM Sans (OFL), 13px, tracked +20, all-caps, weight Regular — neutral enough to carry any name without competing. The date numeral is set oversized at 64px, weight Thin, positioned bottom-left as a structural anchor rather than a decorative flourish — it reads as a coordinate, not an ornament. All live text sits above the WebGL layer in a transparent DOM overlay; it never bakes. Reduced-motion state: typography scales to 16px body, date to 48px; no other change required.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific batch prompt A (botanical, 16 plates): 'Fine-art watercolor on heavy deckled cotton, garden roses and peonies forming an asymmetric arch, eucalyptus and olive sprays, gold-foil flecks caught in raking upper-left light at 35 degrees, white negative space at lower 40% for live text, photographically sharp at centre softening to natural bloom at periphery, no gradients, no digital smoothing, 9:19.5 portrait, 390px minimum legibility, isolated on white.' Magnific batch prompt B (villa, 8 plates): 'Gouache on cold-press paper, Italian villa terrace viewed through a stone colonnade arch, two flanking cypress trees framing a golden-hour hillside, bougainvillea spilling from upper-left, terracotta and lemon-tree detail, light source consistent upper-left 35 degrees casting shadow rightward, centred aperture clear for text, 9:19.5 portrait.' Magnific batch prompt C (deco, 8 plates): 'Dee
proposals.texture: Botanical family: simulated deckled cotton paper tooth — a procedural normal map derived from a scanned paper height field (Plajah-owned or generated via Magnific 'macro paper surface' sub-prompt) applied to the art plate in the WebGL layer, roughness 0.4, so raking light at 35°/22° reads as physical tooth, not a filter. Villa family: cold-press gouache texture, slightly smoother, roughness 0.25, with a faint linen weave from the same normal-map pipeline. Deco family: marble field is a WebGL procedural shader (Simplex noise with vein frequency 0.08, anisotropic along the card's vertical axis), emerald base colour #1B4332, gold vein #C9A84C — the shader is the texture, not an image. Foil shimmer on all three families shares the same reflection vector derived from the 35°/22° light declaration: shimmer angle = atan2(sin(22°), sin(35°)), so a card rotated in the hand reads physically consis
proposals.motion: Sequence governed by a single timing function derived from the light source declaration — the '400–900ms staged plane arrival' is not arbitrary; plane Z-1 (bokeh field) fades in at 0ms, art plate Z0 at 400ms, foreground cut-outs Z+1 at 650ms, live text at 900ms. This is the order light would reveal a physical object emerging from darkness. Parallax on phone tilt: foreground cut-outs gain ±18px at 1.0 sensitivity; art plate ±6px at 0.33; bokeh field ±2px at 0.11 — gain ratios are 1 : 0.33 : 0.11, a geometric series, not tuned by feel. Foil shimmer responds to tilt angle directly: shimmer highlight position = light_vector + tilt_delta * 0.6, clamped to card bounds. Candle flicker (botanical and villa families only): a 0.3Hz Perlin noise modulation on the bokeh layer opacity, amplitude 0.08 — visible as a slow breath, not a flame animation; deco family substitutes a 0.15Hz specular pulse on
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific batch prompt runs (described under imageLogic) return 32 art plates total; editorial selection yields 36 by using two botanical variants per prompt slot. Foreground cut-out elements re-prompted as isolated transparent PNGs, composited in Tela as separate layers. Deco marble is a WebGL fragment shader (Simplex noise + anisotropic vein, written once, parameterised by hue uniform so all 12 deco cards share one shader). Paper normal maps generated via a Magnific macro-texture sub-prompt ('extreme close-up of heavy cotton rag paper, raking light, no colour, greyscale height field') and baked into a 512×512 texture used as a shared asset. All shimmer, bokeh, parallax, and flicker are WebGL uniforms driven by the single light-source declaration; changing the light source azimuth/elevation pair propagates to all downstream parameters without manual re-tuning. Live text is DOM, never
proposals.humanTrace: The editorial selection pressure — which 36 plates from 32+ returns, which foreground elements, which moment in the bokeh breath cycle is the static fallback — is the primary human trace. The paper normal map, even when generated, carries the stochastic topology of rag fibre; no two cards share the same roughness micro-detail because the normal map is applied at different UV offsets per card. The Perlin noise seed for candle flicker is set once per card at generation time and never randomised on load, so the flicker is authored, not procedurally random per session — it is a performance with a fixed score, not an improvisation.
proposals.risk: The risk is that the system reads as cold — that guests feel they are looking at a demo rather than an invitation. The counter-argument is that physical coherence is what makes the weight of letterpress legible on a phone screen: a card that flickers differently every load, or whose shimmer angle is disconnected from its shadow direction, will feel cheaper than paper, not heavier. The bet is that rigour at the system level produces warmth at the surface level, because nothing is arbitrary. If the bet loses, the fix is not to add more decoration but to re-examine whether the timing constants are too mechanical — the Perlin frequency and the plane-arrival curve are the only knobs that govern perceived warmth, and they should be the last thing tuned, not the first.

I reject this because a reveal is a one-time event and this card is opened multiple times, shared as a link preview, loaded on slow mobile data. proposals.title: Light From One Declared Source
proposals.idea: Every plate in the line descends from a single physical logic — a 35° upper-left motivated light source that governs foil shimmer angle, bokeh origin, parallax shadow offset, and candle-flicker falloff simultaneously, so the collection reads as one coherent world rather than thirty-six moods, and every decorative element is traceable to a specific, named material or place rather than a generalised 'romantic' aesthetic.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 phone-native ratio throughout. Each family uses a different internal grid: Family A (watercolour botanicals) uses an asymmetric arch — a single curved spine at 62% of width, botanical mass heavy left-and-low, text zone floating upper-right on open deckled ground; Family B (Italian terraces) uses a strict three-register horizontal — sky, architecture, foreground planting — with text locked to the middle register as if engraved into stone; Family C (art deco emerald) uses a radial symmetry anchored to a central medallion, four-quadrant linework expanding outward, text centred and axis-aligned. Families never cross-contaminate their grids. Twelve plates per family, each plate a geometrically distinct crop or compositional variation within its family's fixed rule.
proposals.typography: Primary: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — the italic for names and venue, the light roman for date and body, set large enough to feel engraved, not printed. Tracking +80 on headlines, +20 on body. All-caps small-caps for the host line only. Secondary: IM Fell English (OFL) for Family A only — its irregular baseline echoes hand-press letterpress and is specific to British printing history, not a generic serif. Family C uses Josefin Sans (OFL) for the deco register lines only — geometric, 1920s-attributed, never mixed into A or B. No face appears in more than one family. Minimum 17px rendered body size at 390px viewport. Live text layer sits above art plate in Tela; never baked.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative prompts directed as follows — Family A prompt: 'Fine-art watercolour on 300gsm Fabriano cold-press cotton, garden roses Rosa centifolia and R. gallica, white peonies Paeonia lactiflora, silver-dollar eucalyptus and Olea europaea olive branch forming an asymmetric arch, loose wet-on-wet technique with visible granulation, gold-leaf flecks physically pressed not digital, deckled paper edge visible lower-left, single directional light source upper-left 35° azimuth casting soft warm shadow, no text, no faces, no trademarked flora cultivar names, 9:19.5 portrait, 16 compositional variants on one grid'; Family B prompt: 'Gouache painting on tinted paper, southern Italian villa terrace, specific reference: Ravello-style arched colonnade, Amalfi coast limestone, terracotta urns with Citrus limon, Bougainvillea spectabilis magenta, Cupressus sempervirens pencil cypress, golden
proposals.texture: Family A: simulated Fabriano cotton-paper tooth via WebGL normal-map displacement — the normal map is procedurally generated from a 512×512 tileable noise field tuned to cold-press paper micro-texture; gold-foil flecks rendered as WebGL metallic patches inheriting 35° specular angle. Family B: lime-washed stone grain on the architecture register, terracotta micro-texture on urns, both procedural. Family C: marble veining is a procedural shader (Worley + Perlin composite), not a photograph of real marble, so no provenance ambiguity; gold linework has a foil-stamp depth simulation via bump offset in the WebGL layer. All texture layers are masks, not baked into the art plate, so Tela can reveal or suppress them per device capability.
proposals.motion: Entrance (0–1.2s): art plate fades from white at 0% opacity to 100% over 600ms — the timing mimics a photographic print emerging in developer, not a UI transition; foreground cut-outs (petals, a cypress branch tip, a constellation arc) are separate transparent layers that drift in 200ms after the plate, moving toward their resting position from 8px below — slow, weighted, as if settling under gravity. Ambient (continuous): parallax on device tilt — foreground cut-outs shift ±12px on X and Y axes relative to the static art plate, creating a depth field; the 35° light source is the origin point for all parallax shadow offsets, so tilting the phone toward the light source brightens foil shimmer and tilting away deepens shadow — the physics are consistent with the declared light. Family A only: a single candle-flicker shader pulses warm light at 0.3Hz with ±4% brightness variance, origin fix
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific batch prompt runs — Run 1 targets Family A (16-plate grid), Run 2 covers Families B and C together (8+8 on one grid). Editorial pass selects 12 plates per family from the returns, rejecting any plate with ambiguous light direction, legibility conflict in the text zone, or culturally unattributable decorative motif. Selected plates are upscaled to 2400×5200px for retina. Foreground cut-outs are isolated from each plate using generative inpainting to produce transparent-background PNG layers — petals, a single cypress, constellation arc segments — these are the parallax elements. WebGL foil and texture shaders are written procedurally in GLSL, parameterised so the 35° azimuth is a single declared constant that all specular, shadow, and shimmer calculations derive from; changing that one value recolours the physics of the entire collection. Tela document structure: Layer 0 art
proposals.humanTrace: The 35° azimuth is a declared editorial decision, documented in the prompt and enforced in the shader constant — it is as traceable as a photographer's stated light setup. The watercolour granulation in Family A is directed, not default: the prompt specifies wet-on-wet technique and Fabriano cold-press, and plates that show flat digital blending are rejected. The star positions in Family C are not decorative scatter — they are Andromeda and Lyra drawn from Bayer catalogue coordinates, which means a researcher made a choice about which sky to show. The candle-flicker frequency (0.3Hz) was chosen to match the measured flicker rate of a beeswax taper in still air, not a generic 'warm glow' preset. These decisions are legible to another maker.
proposals.risk: The 35° constraint will occasionally fight a plate that is genuinely more beautiful with a different light — I will lose some stunning images to the rule. That loss is worth it because a collection that holds one physical logic reads as a designed world; a collection that optimises each plate individually reads as a catalogue. The second risk is that Family B's Italian villa reference is specific to Ravello and the Amalfi limestone vernacular — I have named it exactly so that it cannot slide into a generic 'Mediterranean' that flattens the Campanian, Sicilian, Ligurian, and Dalmatian coasts into one aesthetic. If the team or the client wants a different Italian region, that is a new brief with new specificity, not a palette swap.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will want to pull Family C into full Byzantine gold-on-black and push the constellation motif toward something grander — more stars, more gold, more coverage. proposals.title: The Candlelit Reveal
proposals.idea: Every card is a single theatrical moment — a diorama lit from one motivated source — in which the motion layer does not animate decoration but performs the physics of candlelight discovering a room: the reveal is not an entrance effect, it is the dramatic event itself.
proposals.geometry: Three families, each with a governing spatial logic. Family A (Botanical Arch): a tall portrait stage, 9:19.5, with the floral arch as a proscenium framing deep negative space — flowers at 60% bleed top and sides, the text zone a lit clearing at center-low, as if a candle were placed on a table inside the arch. Family B (Villa Terrazza): a forced-perspective horizon composition — foreground colonnade hard-cropped left and right, mid-ground terrace, deep cypress and hillscape receding to a warm sky; text sits on the terrace as if carved into stone. Family C (Deco Firmament): strict bilateral symmetry, octagonal frame within the rectangle, constellation field as the deepest layer, gold linework frame as mid-layer, marble slab as the text surface; the geometry is load-bearing, not ornamental. All three families share one structural rule: a single implied light source at 35° upper-left that
proposals.typography: Primary display: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — the italic for names, the SC caps for venue and date; the weight contrast within a single optical size does the work that letterpress ink-trap does on paper. Secondary: IM Fell English (OFL) for the body copy block — its deliberate irregularity reads as letterpress impression at small sizes on mobile. No geometric sans anywhere in this line. Case: names in title case italic, all secondary lines in tracked small caps at 80/1000 tracking. Scale: name at 32–36px on 390px canvas, venue at 14px SC, date at 13px SC — hierarchy is operatic, not polite. The type never touches the art plate; it floats in the lit clearing and is set live in Tela.
proposals.imageLogic: All art plates are Magnific generative outputs directed as two prompt grids. Prompt Grid 1 (8 plates, Families A and B): 'Fine-art botanical arch — garden roses, peonies, olive branch, eucalyptus, ranunculus — rendered as high-resolution gouache on 300gsm cold-press cotton, visible paper tooth, wet-edge blooms, gold-foil flecks caught in raking sidelight from upper-left 35°, deckled border visible at bottom edge, deep shadow in arch interior, photographic depth of field, no text, no people, portrait 9:19.5, 8 color variants across warm ivory, dusty sage, blush, antique gold ground — PLUS — Italian villa terrace, golden-hour, arched colonnade foreground hard-cropped, cypress mid-ground, lemon grove, terracotta urns, bougainvillea magenta, gouache texture, same 35° sidelight, stone surface readable at center, 4 variants.' Prompt Grid 2 (8 plates, Family C): 'Art deco symmetrical frame — de
proposals.texture: Paper tooth is simulated at the compositing stage: a procedural grain shader (GLSL, 0.18 opacity multiply) lays fine cold-press fiber texture across the entire canvas — visible at 1:1 on Retina, invisible at thumbnail. Gold foil is a WebGL specular highlight layer masked to the linework paths and bloom edges — it responds to the 35° light vector, brightening on tilt toward source, dimming away. The marble in Family C is a generated tileable texture with genuine vein directionality, not a flat color. Candle flicker is a low-frequency Perlin noise shader (0.3–1.2Hz) modulating the warm fill light in the text clearing — it is subtle enough to be subconscious, dramatic enough that the room feels inhabited.
proposals.motion: The sequence is a curtain-rise in four beats, timed to a guest opening the link — not an autoplay loop, a single unrepeated performance on load, then a living steady state. Beat 1 (0–0.4s): darkness. The plate is present but the WebGL light layer is at zero — the guest sees a silhouette, a shape, a weight. Beat 2 (0.4–1.2s): the motivated light blooms from the upper-left source — not a fade-in, a bloom, as if a candle were carried into the room from off-stage left; foil edges catch first, then the bloom interiors, then the text clearing warms. Beat 3 (1.2–2.0s): the foreground cutout layer drifts forward 8px on a gentle ease — depth arrives after light, because that is how eyes work in a candlelit room. Beat 4 (2.0–2.4s): the text resolves — not a fade, a focus-pull, the Cormorant italic sharpening from 0.6 to 1.0 opacity over 0.4s. Steady state: gyroscope-driven parallax on the cutout l
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids (described above) return 16 distinct art plates. Each plate is composited in a Tela document with five named layers: (1) Art Plate — generated image, static; (2) Grain Shader — GLSL procedural, multiply blend; (3) Foreground Cutouts — generated transparent PNGs, tilt-reactive via DeviceOrientation API; (4) WebGL Effects Mask — foil specular, bokeh, candle flicker, light bloom, all driven by the 35° vector and gyroscope input; (5) Live Text — Tela native, Cormorant Garamond + IM Fell English, names/dates/venues never baked. Reduced-motion: layers 3 and 4 collapse to a static foil-shimmer still, no flicker, no parallax. Load budget: art plate WebP at 85% quality, ~180KB; shaders are inline GLSL, ~8KB; cutout PNGs ~40KB each, lazy-loaded after Beat 2. Total under 400KB before text.
proposals.humanTrace: The grain shader is calibrated by eye against a physical scan of 300gsm Arches cold-press — not sampled, matched by a director looking at both until the fiber scale is right. The candle flicker frequency (0.3–1.2Hz) is set by timing an actual candle with a phone camera and reading the oscillation; the Perlin noise parameters are tuned to that interval. The 35° light vector is a decision, not a default — it is the angle at which late-afternoon Mediterranean sidelight enters a south-facing room with a window at shoulder height, which is the specific quality of light these couples are trying to remember.
proposals.risk: The four-beat unrepeated reveal is a gamble: a guest who opens the link while distracted misses it entirely and sees only the steady state. The counter-argument is that the steady state is itself beautiful — the foil breathes, the parallax gives depth, the candle flickers — and that a reveal which repeats is not a reveal, it is an animation loop, and animation loops are what screensavers do. The other risk is that the Cormorant/IM Fell pairing reads as historically precious rather than contemporary luxury; this is managed by the scale contrast and the live WebGL environment, which no historical precedent has ever had. The risk is worth taking because every alternative — a fade-in, a loop, a parallax-on-scroll — has been done, and the brief asks us to sit beside the best paper stationery studios and win. Paper cannot do a curtain rise. We should do one.

I disagree specifically and not generally: restraint in this brief is not a virtue, it is a category error. proposals.title: One Rule, Thirty-Six Silences
proposals.idea: Every plate in the collection is governed by a single declared light source — its angle, its warmth, its falloff — from which foil direction, bokeh origin, shadow offset, foreground drift axis, and candle flicker phase are all derived, not applied; the visual luxury is not ornament but coherence so total it reads as material weight.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 phone canvas, 390px wide. A single golden-ratio vertical spine divides each plate: art occupies the upper 61.8%, live text the lower 38.2%. No bleeds that fight the ratio. Negative space is load-bearing — the margin is never less than 24px and is never filled. The 36 designs are organized into three families of twelve (botanical, villa, deco) but all twelve within a family share one spatial grammar: the same spine, the same horizon, the same declared light angle of 35°. That angle is the only rule. Everything else is derived from it.
proposals.typography: Primary: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) — italic for names, small-caps for date and venue, tracked to 200 for location lines. Secondary: DM Sans (OFL) — lightweight, 13px, for RSVP and host lines only. No display weight, no decorative alternates. Type is always live Tela text, never baked. Scale contrast is the only typographic gesture: one name at 32px, everything else at 13–15px. The silence between those two sizes is the hierarchy.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative plates directed as physical objects under a 35° warm light source (2700K, described explicitly in every prompt). Botanical family: cotton-rag paper surface carrying pressed pigment, not illustrated — the prompt asks for a photograph of a physical art object that does not exist, so Magnific renders its texture plausibly. Villa family: golden-hour stone and plaster, light raking across terracotta at 35° so shadow depth reads as mass. Deco family: deep emerald mineral surface with gold linework that catches the same 35° as a foil stamping under a single lamp. Each plate is one Magnific draft grid of 8–16 variants; editorial selection is the human act. No plate contains a face, a figure, or a legible word.
proposals.texture: Botanical: simulated 300gsm cotton rag — paper tooth visible under raking 35° light, pigment blooms at fiber edges, deckle implied by falloff not by a drawn border. Villa: warm stucco and worn limestone, no filter grain, texture comes from the light angle alone. Deco: cold-pressed emerald mineral (malachite logic) with hairline gold at 0.5px — the foil is a WebGL layer driven by the same 35° vector, not a texture map. Grain is physically motivated, never applied as a post-process veil.
proposals.motion: One motion law: everything that moves obeys the declared light source. Phase 1 — load: the plate fades in from the light side (top-right at 35°), not from center, over 600ms ease-out. Phase 2 — idle: foreground botanical or architectural cut-out drifts ±4px on the 35° axis only, responding to gyroscope tilt; the drift axis never changes because the light source never changes. Phase 3 — foil: WebGL shimmer activates on the hairline gold elements, its specular peak always at 35° regardless of tilt, so the foil feels physically consistent. Phase 4 — candle (botanical and villa families only): a single bokeh particle origin sits at the light-source position; flicker is a 0.3Hz sine on opacity, not position. Nothing moves that is not already implied by stillness. Reduced-motion: all drift and flicker collapse to a single 400ms fade; foil shimmer becomes a static specular highlight baked into
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific draft-grid prompts per family (botanical, villa, deco), each returning 8–16 plates at flat cost — 36 usable plates selected editorially from roughly 48 candidates. Prompt language specifies: surface material, light angle (35°, warm, single source, no fill), shadow direction, color temperature, and the instruction that no text, face, or trademarked element appears. Foreground cut-outs are generated as separate alpha-channel elements using the same light logic, composited in Tela. WebGL layer (foil shimmer, bokeh, flicker) is a shared shader across all 36 designs, parameterized by: light angle (constant 35°), color temperature (per family), and shimmer intensity (per design). The shader is written once; the 36 designs are instances. Typography is live Tela text throughout.
proposals.humanTrace: Editorial selection from the draft grid — the act of choosing which eight of sixteen plates carry the right silence. And the prompt itself: the decision to name 35° as the single governing axiom, to refuse independent bokeh origins, to hold the foil vector constant even when a different angle would be more dramatic. The restraint is the trace. The one rule that was not broken across 36 plates is the sign that a person was present.
proposals.risk: The collection risks reading as cold — thirty-six variations of the same restraint may feel institutional to guests expecting the warmth of a paper suite. The counter-argument: warmth is in the light temperature and material simulation, not in decorative density; a 2700K single source on cotton rag is candlelight, not a dashboard. The deeper risk is that the single-rule system becomes legible as a system — guests may perceive the family resemblance as template-ness rather than collection-ness. This is worth it because the alternative — thirty-six independently art-directed cards — is not a luxury line; it is a catalogue. Coherence is the luxury.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will argue that thirty-six designs governed by one angle is not a collection but a constraint, and that emotional weight requires accumulation — more gold, more depth, more gesture. I say the weight of a letterpress card comes from what is not there: the unprinted cotton, the shadow beside the type. The Dramatist adds until something happens. disputes.objection: The golden-ratio spine is stated as a structural act, but dividing every plate by the same 61.8/38.2 proportion and calling the result a 'rule' is not structure — it is a single measurement repeated thirty-six times without counterpoint or consequence; the Parthenon does not deploy one ratio and stop there, it subjects that ratio to column spacing, entablature height, and stylobate curvature so that every member tests and confirms every other. A governing constraint that never meets resistance cannot be called load-bearing. What this proposal calls silence I would call abdication: the negative space is preserved, but nothing hangs from it, nothing earns its rest against anything else, and a
disputes.concession: The insistence that the 35° light source govern drift axis, foil vector, and bokeh origin without exception — that no element be permitted an independent motivation — is precisely the cantus firmus discipline I have always demanded, and it is correctly named as the structural act it is.

disputes.objection: The restraint is performing purity, not risking anything — when your 'human trace' is the act of not breaking a rule across 36 plates, you have made the absence of a decision into the decision, and I cannot see a human hand in that; I see a policy. The foil vector held constant 'even when a different angle would be more dramatic' is not discipline, it is refusal dressed as conviction, and there is no evidence in the work of what it cost to make that refusal — no bleed, no resistance mark, nothing that could survive being photocopied four times. Silence is only load-bearing when something was silenced; this silence was never in danger.
disputes.concession: The one place the restraint earns its keep is the 32px name against 13px everything-else — that gap is a real decision with a real edge to it, and the 'silence between those two sizes is the hierarchy' is the most honest sentence in the proposal.

disputes.objection: The candlelit reveal is a sequence of theatrical states, not a system — Beat 1 through Beat 4 are scripted in clock-time like a film cut, which means the behaviour is authored, not derived; if the guest opens the link in a bright room versus a dark one, if they arrive at second three instead of zero, the whole dramatic logic collapses because it was never a rule, it was a schedule. 'Darkness, then bloom, then depth, then text' is a director's storyboard dressed as interaction design, and a storyboard is not a behaviour. disputes.concession: The insistence that the text float in a lit clearing — a zone of warm fill derived from the candle position — is the one spatial move here that functions as a rule rather than decoration: the text zone is not placed by eye, it is where the light lands, and that is exactly the kind of derivable conse

disputes.objection: The 'one rule' is presented as if a 35° azimuth is culturally neutral — a physical law that belongs to no one and therefore belongs to everyone. But the botanical, villa, and deco vocabularies are not neutral placeholders: each of them carries a specific visual inheritance, and declaring a single geometric constraint across all three flattens the question of where those forms come from into a problem of light-angle arithmetic. The Minimalist calls the restraint a human trace, but restraint is not the same as attribution — you can be perfectly silent about whose garden, whose terrace, whose mineral surface you are invoking, and the silence is not ethical, it is just quiet.
disputes.concession: The insistence that grain be physically motivated rather than applied as a post-process veil is exactly right, and I will carry that discipline into my own direction.

disputes.objection: The golden-ratio spine divided into 61.8% art and 38.2% text is not a spatial decision — it is a formula that has been mistaken for one; when the same geometry governs a pressed-botanical plate, a raking-stone villa, and a cold emerald deco field, the proportion becomes wallpaper, not architecture, and the 'silence' the direction celebrates is not earned restraint but the absence of a decision about what each family actually feels like in the body. The 4px drift axis is not drama — it is a tremor, and a tremor is not the same thing as breath. When the Minimalist says 'nothing moves that is not already implied by stillness,' I hear a dramatist refusing to pull the rope, and calling the darkne
disputes.concession: The insistence that grain be physically motivated by the 35° light angle rather than applied as a post-process veil is exactly right — that single discipline separates a coherent material world from a mood filter, and I would hold every direction on this team to it.

disputes.objection: The candlelit reveal is four beats of decoration performing emotion — darkness, bloom, drift, focus-pull — each one an effect added to explain the feeling to a guest who should be allowed to feel it without stage direction; by Beat 4 the card has spent 2.4 seconds telling you it is beautiful before you have seen whether it is. The Perlin candle-flicker, the bloom bloom bloom, the curtain-rise — every layer is an argument for atmosphere, and a card that argues for its own atmosphere does not have one.
disputes.concession: The one structural decision I will not argue against: naming the 35° vector as the single physical law from which foil, parallax, and flicker are all derived — that is a governing axiom, not a mood, and it is correct.

synthesis.direction: Three families — Botanical Arch, Villa Terrazza, Deco Firmament — each governed by a single motivated light source at 35° upper-left, which is the declared axiom before any image is generated. Every plate is produced via two Magnific batch-prompt grids (16 plates each), specifying substrate, light azimuth, and a cleared text zone; foreground cut-outs are a separate transparent-background pass composited in Tela as tilt-reactive parallax layers. The motion sequence is a one-time curtain-rise on load — darkness, light bloom from upper-left, depth arrival, text resolve — followed by a living steady state of gyroscope parallax, foil shimmer locked to the 35° vector, and a 0.3Hz candle-flicker on the bokeh layer; the steady state is the primary experience, the reveal is the opening gift. Typography is Cormorant Garamond (OFL) for all display — italic for names, small-caps for venue and date — with IM Fell English (OFL) for body copy in Botanical and Villa, carrying the letterpress-impression register at mobile scale; all text is live Tela, never baked, minimum 17px rendered body at 390px.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The Classical Mind's insistence that the proportional canon be declared in writing before the first prompt is submitted — specifically, that the text-clearing zone is structurally enforced by the grid rather than placed by eye in post — must survive. The 35° light source is the axiom; the text zone is where the light lands, not where the editor decided it looked good.
synthesis.editorCut: The Futurist removed the Baroque's four-beat clock-time scripting as a fixed schedule and replaced it with a derived timing law: plane arrival order follows depth-from-light (bokeh field first, art plate second, foreground cut-outs third, text last), with durations set by a single easing curve, not by authored beat-counts. This means a guest who arrives mid-sequence sees a coherent physical state, not a broken storyboard. The Futurist also cut IM Fell English from the Deco family — its irregular
synthesis.openDecision: Do you want the curtain-rise reveal to play once per session and never repeat — so the guest who shares the link and reopens it sees only the living steady state — or should it replay on every fresh load, accepting that repeat viewers will experience it as an animation rather than an event?
synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team split cleanly on one question: is the motion layer a performance or a behaviour? The Baroque Dramatist argued for a single unrepeated curtain-rise — darkness, then candlelight blooming from upper-left, then depth, then names — because a reveal that loops is a screensaver. The Futurist pushed back hard, calling the four-beat sequence a director's storyboard rather than interaction design: if a guest arrives at second three, the dramatic logic collapses because it was never a rule, just a schedule. I took the Baroque's side on the experience and the Futurist's side on the mechanism — the reveal plays once, but its timing is derived from the depth-plane order the declared light would logically illuminate, not from authored beat-counts. That gives us the emotional event the Baroque wanted and the physical coherence the Futurist demanded.

The lead philosophy is the Baroque: three families, one motivated light source at 35° upper-left, a cleared candlelit text zone that is structurally placed by where the light lands. The Classical Mind's counterpoint kept us honest — the text zone is enforced by the grid before any image is generated, not adjusted by eye afterward. That discipline is the difference between a designed collection and a curated mood board.

The Radical Minimalist and the Rebellious Hand were both set aside. The Minimalist's single-rule restraint is correct as a system principle — and the team accepted the 35° axiom as the governing constraint across all 36 plates — but the 4px drift and the 61.8/38.2 spine, applied identically to pressed botanicals, raking stone, and cold emerald marble, produces coherence without warmth. The Baroque earns the warmth through motivated light and material simulation; the single axiom is still there, it just has more to govern. The Rebellious Hand's misregister concept is genuinely distinct and commercially risky in the right way, but a luxury wedding line cannot ask its sales surface to explain why the card is not aligned.

One decision remains yours. The curtain-rise is designed as a one-time event — the guest who opens the link fresh gets the performance; the guest who returns sees the living steady state of shimmer, parallax, and candle breath. That is the more defensible artistic position. But if you believe most guests will open the link more than once — forwarding it, showing it to family — then replay
